# Your Quarto project, live in the browser.

::: {.lead}
Quarto Hub renders as you type. You write in the source or directly in the rendered page, and either way it's the same `.qmd`. When you want input, you share a link: comments and edits land in your project, not in a PDF someone emailed back.
:::

::: {.hero-actions}
[Open Hub](https://quarto-hub.com){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg role="button"}

## Best for markdown-first projects

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.hub-card}
### Websites and docs
The whole project: file tree, outline, every page rendered as you edit it.
:::
::: {.hub-card}
### Meeting notes
One `.qmd` the whole team types into during the call. It's rendered before the call ends.
:::
::: {.hub-card}
### Slides
revealjs decks, edited and previewed in place. Your co-presenter gets the link, not a PDF.
:::
:::

Anyone with the link can open the project, read it, and comment. They don't need an account or a Quarto install. You sign in with Google to create and own projects.

:::
:::

::: {.content-block #coming-soon}

<span class="eyebrow">Coming soon</span>

## Next

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.hub-card .soon}
### Code execution
R and Python cells render in Hub, so your reports join your docs and slides.
:::
::: {.hub-card .soon}
### Positron
Open the Hub project in Positron. Your edits and the browser's merge.
:::
::: {.hub-card .soon}
### Agents
Point Claude or any MCP client at the project. It edits the same files, and every change stays in the history.
:::
:::

Hub is built so that whoever has the project open, a teammate, an agent, or you in a different editor, is working on the same source with the same history.

:::

::: {.alt-background}
::: {.content-block}

<span class="eyebrow">Built on Quarto 2</span>

## The engine underneath

Rendering in the browser as you type takes a faster Quarto. That is Quarto 2: the engine rewritten in Rust.
